subject: Request: temporary latency-floor exception & rate fairness window — SaaSCloud launch
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@saascloud.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@saascloud.com
Date: 2026-09-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — launch week latency window and fairness policy

Hi Nikhil,

We're ramping to GA the week of Oct 4th and have a couple of time-boxed requirements from our SRE and product teams. During two 3-hour launch windows (expected traffic spike ~4x baseline) we need: 1) a temporary increase to our burst rate limit for the API key used by our public endpoints, and 2) an exemption from Redwood's fairness policy for that key so critical control-plane calls (model selection + frontend tokenization) don't get throttled.

We understand permanent exceptions are not possible, but a controlled, auditable carveout for launch windows would solve an operational risk for us. Attached is our launch plan and the time windows. Can you confirm if Redwood can support an SLA rider / temporary latency-floor guarantee for those periods?

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform, SaaSCloud
[attachment: SaaSCloud_launch_plan.pdf (PDF)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@saascloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — launch week latency window and fairness policy

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up and for the plan. Short answer: we can often support time-boxed exceptions but need to coordinate capacity, impact on multi-tenant fairness, and a temporary SLO addendum.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben (CC) to confirm available burst capacity for Oct 4–6 windows and any uplift pricing.
- Marissa to confirm contractual approach (SLA rider / limited amendment) and whether legal needs a redline.
- We (Redwood infra ops) will require the exact production key(s), the ingress IP ranges, and a short rollback plan.

To be transparent, exemptions from fairness throttling are allowed only with an explicit pricing and capacity reservation — otherwise we risk impacting adjacent tenants. If you can share the exact call pattern (tokens/sec, percent of model calls that are control-plane), our infra team will simulate the impact.

I'll also attach a proposed template for a short SLA rider and a checklist for the ops runbook.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_sla_rider.docx (DOCX)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@saascloud.com>, ops@saascloud.com
Date: 2026-09-29T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — launch week latency window and fairness policy

Thanks Nikhil/Elena — ran quick capacity checks with infra. Summary:
- We have a block of reserved burst capacity (NVIDIA A100-backed pool) we can assign for a short window, up to ~3.8x baseline for a single customer if committed 48h in advance.
- To keep fairness intact, we implement a namespaced priority token pool tied to the SaaSCloud API key for the stated windows. That pool is isolated from general fairshare buckets.
- Pricing: one-time surge fee (covers reserved GPUs + priority tokens) + prorated per-token usage. I'll send a formal quote once terms are agreed.

Operational asks before we commit: exact UTC windows (we need to set policy rules), list of API keys, and a test replay of your peak pattern in staging (we can run a 30m simulation). If you want a guaranteed latency floor (e.g., p95 < 200ms) during the windows, we need the replay and an acceptance test.

Proposed internal timeline: confirm by EOD 2026-09-30 to finalize scheduling and billing.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@saascloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — launch week latency window and fairness policy

Elena — thanks, all. Recap and immediate asks so we can lock this down today: 
1) Please confirm the exact UTC windows you want (we have tentative Oct 4 16:00–19:00 UTC and Oct 5 02:00–05:00 UTC from the plan).
2) Share the production API key(s) to bind to the priority token pool and the staging replay artifact (or give us a signed URL to a tarball).
3) Approve the temporary SLA rider draft (attached) and the one-time surge fee outlined below so finance can issue an invoice.

Attached is the edited SLA rider with a 72-hour automatic rollback clause, and a brief runbook for escalation during the window. If you approve in writing, we'll:
- Schedule the reserved pool and priority token mapping (48h notice required).
- Run a 30m staging replay with you (we'll provide the replay harness).
- Execute the SLA rider amendment and invoice the surge fee.

If this looks good, please reply "APPROVE" and paste the keys (or a secure upload link) and we'll take it from there. Happy to hop on a quick call if you'd prefer.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
Contact: +1 (415) 555-0198
[attachment: proposed_sla_rider.docx (DOCX), SaaSCloud_launch_plan.pdf (PDF)]
